decisions.title: Publish an uncertain finding?
decisions.text: The detection has been verified once. You can publish a preliminary report now, or keep investigating quietly.

options.label: Publish preliminary report
options.note: +2 reputation now. If the final conclusion disagrees you must retract (-3 reputation).

decisions.title: Prioritise this investigation over routine research?
decisions.text: The characterisation is demanding. Redirecting the laboratory will speed the investigation but slow ordinary analysis.

options.label: Prioritise for 30 days
options.note: Evidence from new steps is 10% more reliable; research points from analysis are 20% lower for 30 days.

decisions.title: Send an autonomous probe or a crewed mission?
decisions.text: The source needs on-site data. A probe is cheap and expendable; a crewed mission gets better data but puts people at risk.

options.label: Autonomous probe
options.note: Costs 400 RC. No risk to people.

options.label: Crewed mission
options.note: Costs 1200 RC. Better evidence (+12% reliability) but crew morale drops.

decisions.title: Preserve the evidence or run a destructive experiment?
decisions.text: A destructive test could resolve the question, but if it fails the best sample is lost for good.

options.label: Run the experiment
options.note: Large evidence gain on success; 30% chance to lose the best evidence item.

options.label: Preserve the evidence
options.note: Safe. The sample is archived for future methods.

decisions.title: Reveal the discovery or keep it secret?
decisions.text: Evidence points to a fictional intelligent source. Announce it to civilization, or maintain secrecy while you learn more?

options.label: Maintain secrecy
options.note: No reward now. About 1 in 3 chance the secret leaks within 4 months, costing 3 reputation.
